channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov to Visit South Korea for Official Trip
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov will undertake an official visit to South Korea from September 15-18, accepting an invitation from President Lee Jae-myung. The trip includes participation in the first "Central Asia - Korea" summit in Seoul, where the Seoul Declaration is expected. Bilateral talks with South Korean leadership and the signing of economic and investment documents are also planned.

item.title: Antimonopoly Service Warns of Investment Scams Promising High Returns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's antimonopoly service has warned citizens about advertisements offering high guaranteed annual returns of up to 20-30% on investments and loans without necessary licenses. The service issued a warning after a request from the Financial Supervision Authority, noting such offers are spread on social media. The law prohibits guaranteeing future returns for financial services.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov to Visit South Korea for Official Trip
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov will undertake an official visit to South Korea from September 15-18, accepting an invitation from President Lee Jae-myung. The trip includes participation in the first "Central Asia - Korea" summit in Seoul, where the Seoul Declaration is expected. Bilateral talks with South Korean leadership and the signing of economic and investment documents are also planned.

item.title: Remote Sensing Center to be Established in Dushanbe
item.description: Tajikistan's Communications Service and China's Great Wall Industry Corporation (CGWIC) discussed cooperation in space technologies, including establishing a National Remote Sensing Data Center in Dushanbe. The center aims to significantly contribute to monitoring natural and environmental processes, assessing glaciers, water resources, and disaster impacts. Both sides expressed interest in further collaboration.

item.title: Over 1.4 kg of Drugs Seized from Two Men in Osh Region
item.description: Police in Kyrgyzstan's Osh region arrested two men and seized over 1.4 kilograms of hashish and opium. A 36-year-old foreign national was found with 1 kg of hashish, leading to the arrest of a 27-year-old accomplice who had 324 grams of hashish and 137 grams of opium. A criminal case is underway.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet Plans Meat Market Intervention to Curb Prices
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet plans to increase its livestock herd to 10,000 heads to supply meat directly to the market and control prices. The initiative aims to reduce intermediaries between producers and consumers. Food trucks have already been introduced to sell meat at affordable prices, with further steps to streamline the supply chain.

item.title: Uzbekistan citizens offered 200 construction jobs in Germany with 2500 Euro monthly salary
item.description: Uzbekistan's Migration Agency and Germany's RRG AG are recruiting construction specialists for 200 positions in Germany, offering a monthly salary of 2500 Euros. Applicants aged 18-39 need vocational education and at least two years of experience. The program includes free German language courses up to B1 level and covers visa and flight costs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares unified rules for public service employees handling citizen applications
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is developing unified rules for public service employees who process applications and issue results for state and municipal services. The proposed regulations aim to prevent officials from demanding extra documents, imposing intermediaries, or accepting gifts. Employees must provide clear information, explain procedures, and communicate respectfully. Training and professional appearance are also mandated.

item.title: CSTO 'Border-2025' drills begin in Kazakhstan with Tajik military participation
item.description: The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) 'Border-2025' exercises have commenced in Kazakhstan's Koktal training ground, involving approximately 1,500 military personnel from Tajikistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan. The drills, running until September 18, will focus on combat operations against illegal armed groups and mountain/desert conditions, according to the CSTO.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's correctional facilities hold 5,854 individuals
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's prisons and pre-trial detention centers currently house 5,854 individuals, according to Nurlan Sarchaev, First Deputy Chairman of the State Penitentiary Service. Approximately 60 percent of inmates are fit for work, with about 3,800 engaged in labor. Around 1,200 individuals, including those with disabilities, over 65, and minors, are not assigned work.

item.title: Average salary in Kyrgyzstan reached 54,864 soms in January-July 2026
item.description: The average salary in Kyrgyzstan for January-July 2026 was 54,864 soms, according to the National Statistical Committee. In July 2026, the average monthly nominal wage across all sectors increased by 28.5% year-on-year. Real wage growth, accounting for 11.5% inflation, was approximately 17%. The number of registered unemployed decreased by 16.3%.

item.title: Korean Company to Invest $100 Million in Uzbekistan for Robot Factory Construction
item.description: A Korean company plans to invest $100 million in Uzbekistan to build a robot manufacturing plant. This initiative is part of broader plans for joint projects in artificial intelligence, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, and other high-tech sectors with South Korea.

item.title: Tajikistan Delegation Attends CIS Interpol Heads Meeting in Minsk
item.description: A delegation from Tajikistan's Interpol National Central Bureau participated in a meeting of CIS Interpol heads in Minsk, Belarus, from September 8-10. Discussions focused on strengthening international cooperation, enhancing NCB effectiveness, and expanding information exchange to combat transnational crime, including cybercrime and terrorism.

item.title: Kazakhstan Hosts AI & Digital Bridge 2026 Forum with Global Tech Leaders
item.description: Kazakhstan is fostering an open tech ecosystem and seeking international collaboration for its Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence. The AI MONTH event culminates in the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum in Astana, attracting global companies like NVIDIA and General Atlantic to discuss AI infrastructure and investment.

item.title: Central Asian CSTO Forces Begin Active Phase of 'Rubezh-2026' Joint Exercise in Kazakhstan
item.description: The active phase of the joint exercise "Rubezh-2026" with the Collective Rapid Deployment Forces of the Central Asian region has begun at the Koktal training ground in Kazakhstan. The exercise focuses on combatting illegal armed groups and is conducted amid regional instability.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Launch Two Waste-to-Energy Plants by Year-End
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch two waste-to-energy plants by the end of this year, with six such projects involving Chinese companies scheduled for 2026-2027. These projects aim to process 3.6 million tons of waste annually, generating 1.6 billion kWh of electricity and improving the ecological situation.

item.title: Number of Entrepreneurs in Tajikistan's Sughd Region Increased by 19% in Four Years
item.description: The number of entrepreneurs in Tajikistan's Sughd region grew by 19% over the past four years, reaching 135,800 individuals as of July 1. The private sector accounts for over 90% of industrial and agricultural production, construction, transport, trade, and services. Approximately $4 billion in foreign and domestic investments were attracted to the region.

item.title: Emomali Rahmon to attend Central Asia-Korea summit in Seoul
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon will travel to Seoul to participate in the Central Asia-Korea summit of heads of state. The event is scheduled for September 16 and will include leaders from South Korea and five Central Asian nations.

item.title: Russian and Tajik universities discuss expanding cooperation and promoting Russian language
item.description: Russian Deputy Minister of Science and Higher Education Konstantin Mogilevsky met with the rector of the Russian-Tajik (Slavic) University (RSU) in Dushanbe to discuss RSU's development. The meeting focused on enhancing cooperation with Russian universities, promoting the Russian language, and developing joint educational programs. Prospects for creating new programs and a Center for Professional Competencies were also considered.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Interior and Education Ministries enhance security measures for new school year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry and Education Ministry are increasing security measures around educational institutions as the 2026-2027 academic year begins on September 15. Law enforcement will ensure student safety on roads, monitor traffic rules, and conduct preventive work. Drivers are urged to be cautious near schools, and parents are advised to discuss road safety with their children.

item.title: Lawyer seeks public help to cover damages for convicted Kyrgyz nephrologist
item.description: The lawyer for convicted Kyrgyz nephrologist Nasira Beyshebaeva is appealing for public assistance to help her pay over 2 million soms in damages awarded to a patient's mother. The doctor was sentenced to three years in prison. The lawyer stated the sum is unaffordable for the doctor and provided a bank account for donations.

item.title: Chubak aжы Jalilov Awarded 'People's Hero' Title Posthumously
item.description: Chubak aжы Jalilov has been posthumously awarded the highest title of 'People's Hero' of Kyrgyzstan. President Sadyr Japarov presented the award to his son, Abdullah Jalilov. The title recognizes his significant contribution to religious education and cultural traditions.

item.title: CIS Penitentiary Service Heads Convene in Kazan for Regular Meeting
item.description: The Council of Heads of Penitentiary Services of CIS member states held a regular meeting in Kazan on September 11, 2026. Representatives from Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan attended. The meeting focused on strengthening stability and security within the CIS.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Building 'New Silk Road' with South Korea
item.description: In an article published in South Korea's The Chosun Daily, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed establishing a 'New Silk Road' with South Korea. He analyzed historical ties, current strategic partnership, and future priorities, advocating for a 21st-century route through advanced industries and transport corridors.

item.title: Juma Odina: A courageous Tajik writer criticized Communist Party policies during the Soviet era
item.description: Juma Odina was a courageous Tajik writer who criticized Communist Party policies during the Soviet era. His novel 'Guzashti ayyom' faced backlash, leading to the burning of 14,000 copies. He was expelled from the Writers' Union and died in Dushanbe in 1982.

item.title: Uzbek electricians and concrete workers sought for jobs in Serbia with salaries up to 1500 euros
item.description: Serbia is offering 1,000 construction jobs for Uzbek citizens as part of preparations for the 2027 EXPO exhibition. Electricians can earn 1000-1500 euros monthly, while concrete workers will receive 700-1200 euros. Accommodation and food are provided.

item.title: ABank Receives High Rating from Independent Sustainable Fitch
item.description: ABank has received an 'Excellent' rating from the international rating agency Sustainable Fitch for its Green Financing Program, developed with support from the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI). This independent assessment confirms the program's high compliance with international capital market principles and sustainable financing standards, paving the way for ABank's entry into the international green bond market.

item.title: Uzbekistan sees rise in court cases of violence against women
item.description: Uzbek courts processed 2,018 criminal cases related to violence and harassment against women in the first half of 2026, a 65.7% increase from the previous year. Of these, 1,624 individuals were convicted, and 2,146 women were identified as victims.

item.title: Saudi oil exports at risk as global supply could drop by 4%
item.description: Saudi oil exports face risks, with potential for a 4% drop in global supply, according to Reuters. The Tadawul All Share Index (TASI) fell 1.3% on September 13, marking its largest daily decline since early April.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host International Forum on Sustainable Tourism Development
item.description: Dushanbe will host the "Dushanbe International Tourism Exhibition – 2026" and the International Forum "City Integration in Realizing Sustainable Tourism Opportunities" from September 24-26. An organizing committee has been formed to manage these events, aimed at developing sustainable tourism, expanding inter-city cooperation, attracting investment, and promoting Tajikistan's tourism potential.

item.title: UK Ambassador: Uzbekistan's Independence Crucial for Britain, Discusses Reforms and Regional Security
item.description: As his mission concludes, UK Ambassador Timothy Smart reflects on his tenure in Uzbekistan (2023-2026). In his final interview, he discussed trade, investment, education, and security changes. Smart emphasized the importance of Uzbekistan's independence and territorial integrity for the UK and outlined prospects for cooperation with the Central Asian region.

item.title: 151 Officials Dismissed for Poor Handling of Public Appeals; 150 Others Face Administrative Action
item.description: Over an eight-month period, 151 officials were dismissed for shortcomings in handling public appeals, while another 150 state employees faced administrative responsibility. The most significant errors and deficiencies were identified in the sectors of employment, community affairs, public-legal services, and healthcare.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 20-year-old man and accomplice sentenced for grandmother's murder and arson
item.description: A 20-year-old man and his accomplice in Uzbekistan's Baghdod district have been sentenced for murdering his grandmother and burning her home. The court found the grandson guilty of murder, theft, and property destruction, sentencing him to 17 years imprisonment.

item.title: Russia strikes train traveling from Ukraine to Poland; Boris Johnson's train also at risk
item.description: A train traveling from Ukraine to Poland was struck by a Russian drone attack near Warsaw. A special train carrying European diplomats, including Boris Johnson, was also in the vicinity. Poland's Prime Minister warned of escalating tensions.

item.title: Water Supply Interruption in Bishkek Affects Three Residential Areas and City Parts
item.description: Bishkekvodokanal announced a drinking water supply suspension in parts of Bishkek on September 16, from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. The outage will impact specific streets and the Altyn Ordo, Kara-Zhygach, and Politseysky Gorodok residential areas due to maintenance at the Kontrrezervuary water intake facility.

item.title: BRICS Summit: Putin, Xi Jinping, and Modi Advocate for a New World Order
item.description: Leaders of Russia, China, and India are pushing for a new world order, according to BBC reporting on the BRICS summit in New Delhi. Indian Prime Minister Modi stated that BRICS nations should increasingly shape global rules rather than follow them, emphasizing the role of the Global South and advocating for UN Security Council reform.

item.title: Kazakh Tenge Reaches Yearly Highs, Russian Ruble Also Rises: Currency Rates for September 14
item.description: The Russian ruble and Kazakh tenge have reached monthly and yearly highs, respectively. The euro and Chinese yuan have slightly decreased in value, while the US dollar's exchange rate remained unchanged. These figures are based on data from the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan and Bishkek exchange offices.

item.title: German companies in Uzbekistan paid 5.1 trillion soms in taxes over eight months
item.description: German companies operating in Uzbekistan paid 5.1 trillion soms in taxes during the first eight months of the year. The Tax Committee reported this figure is an 8% increase compared to the previous year. Approximately 300 German companies currently employ 46,600 people in the republic.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Reports 34% Increase in Bank Deposits Over One Year
item.description: Bank deposits in Uzbekistan have increased by 34% in one year, according to the Central Bank. The regulator stated that this significant growth contributes to the expansion of financial resources, with the largest portion deposited for terms up to one year.

item.title: Uzbek President Emphasizes Unity and Reforms Amid Global Risks
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stressed the importance of national unity, peace, and accelerating reforms in Tashkent. He highlighted the need to understand national identity and the value of labor and citizen satisfaction with reforms. He also linked internal reforms to seeking international partners.
